page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.tiny is an entry-level virtual instance belonging to the Shared server family. Powered by a KVM hypervisor and an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, the configuration allocates 1 dedicated vCPU across a single physical core and single thread. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets. Memory capacity is fixed at 1.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU hardware, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not bundled.

Performance benchmarks place the instance within lower-tier scoring brackets, consistent with its compact single-core resource allocation. The instance scored 1087.59 in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng workloads. PassMark evaluations produced an overall CPU score of 1316.17, an extended instructions score of 1194.42, an encryption score of 406.98, and a memory score of 690.99. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrated 81.03 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached blocks, with uncached 256 MB read and write speeds registering 8.5 GB/sec and 7.1 GB/sec respectively. In service-oriented workloads, the platform recorded 1.43 million Redis SET operations per second and 0.93 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

With its minimal resource footprint, the instance presents clear engineering tradeoffs between density and execution headroom. The low memory ceiling of 1.0 GB restricts concurrency and rules out in-memory caching or heavy runtime stacks. However, the dedicated core allocation ensures predictable behavior within its baseline envelope, making it an economical option for lightweight operations. Appropriate use cases include basic network proxies, lightweight background daemons, automation runners, simple monitoring agents, and low-traffic development or testing environments.

The hardware lacks dedicated local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on remote disk infrastructure for persistent storage. In benchmark evaluations, the instance operates within entry-level performance brackets, recording 1087.59 in stress-ng compute tests and a PassMark CPU score of 1316.17. This minimalist hardware configuration offers a cost-conscious footprint designed for lightweight utility tasks, development environments, low-traffic web endpoints, and minimal background daemons that require modest compute without significant memory demands.
